title: Shopify vs Adobe Commerce Platform Comparison: An APAC View
summary: A practical Shopify vs Adobe Commerce platform comparison from an Asia-Pacific perspective: TCO, localisation, ERP integration, and a five-question framework.
body_markdown:
**Quick Answer:** Shopify Plus suits most APAC retailers: faster multi-market rollout, lower total cost, and non-technical change velocity. Adobe Commerce suits dealer networks and complex B2B pricing that must live in-platform — but only if you can fund permanent engineering. Complexity type, not company size, decides.


---


The honest starting position for any Shopify vs Adobe Commerce platform comparison in Asia-Pacific is this: the platform decision matters far less than most boards think, and the operating model around it matters far more. I have watched retailers spend nine months choosing between the two, then lose the next eighteen months because nobody owned the product data, the ERP integration, or the market-by-market payment stack. The platform is maybe 20% of the outcome.


*Related reading:*[Ecommerce Platform Cost & Speed Comparison 2026: APAC Verdict](https://branch8.com/posts/ecommerce-platform-cost-speed-comparison-2026-apac)


*Related reading:*[AI-Powered E-Commerce Fashion Photography Product Images in APAC](https://branch8.com/posts/ai-powered-ecommerce-fashion-photography-product-images-apac)


That said, the 20% still has to be right. And the calculus in Hong Kong, Singapore, Kuala Lumpur, Taipei or Sydney is genuinely different from the calculus in Ohio or Manchester — different payment rails, different logistics carriers, different tax regimes, different channel behaviour. Most comparison articles are written from a US or UK vantage point and quietly assume Stripe, USPS, and a single currency. That assumption breaks the moment you sell into five ASEAN markets.


## The Verdict, Up Front


**Choose Shopify Plus if** your commercial model is direct-to-consumer or light B2B, you sell across several APAC markets with different currencies and payment habits, you want your merchandising team shipping changes without a developer, and you value speed-to-market over total control of the codebase. This covers the majority of retail, F&B, and brand-led businesses we see across the region.


*Related reading:*[Salesforce Marketing Cloud AI Agents + CDP: An APAC B2B Playbook](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-marketing-cloud-ai-agents-cdp-apac-b2b)


*Related reading:*[Salesforce Genie CDP Competitive Advantages 2026: APAC Verdict](https://branch8.com/posts/salesforce-genie-cdp-competitive-advantages-2026)


*Related reading:*[Framework Linux Laptop Sales Outpacing Windows Demand in APAC](https://branch8.com/posts/framework-linux-laptop-sales-windows-demand-apac)


**Choose Adobe Commerce if** your commercial model has irreducible complexity that lives *inside* the commerce layer — dealer-specific pricing tiers, quote-to-order workflows, configurable industrial products, ERP-driven inventory logic across dozens of warehouses — and you have, or will fund, a permanent engineering capability. Not a launch project. A permanent capability.


**Choose neither** if your primary market is Greater China or Southeast Asia social commerce and your traffic comes from LINE, WhatsApp, Instagram DMs, and livestream. Regional platforms like SHOPLINE are built around that behaviour in a way neither Western platform is.


The rest of this piece explains how to arrive at that verdict for your own business rather than borrowing mine.


## A Comparison Framework That Survives Contact With Procurement


Most comparison charts score the two platforms on features. Features are the least durable input — both vendors ship quarterly, and whatever gap exists today is partially closed within a year. Score them on these five axes instead, in this order of weight.


### 1. Total cost of ownership over 36 months, not licence fees


Shopify publishes its own comparison claiming Adobe Commerce carries roughly 42% higher implementation and setup costs and 42% higher platform fees on average ([Shopify](https://www.shopify.com/plus) ). Treat vendor-published comparisons as directional, not neutral. But the structural point holds and is easy to verify independently: Adobe Commerce is licence-plus-hosting-plus-build-plus-maintenance, while Shopify Plus is subscription-plus-apps-plus-build.


Shopify Plus pricing starts in the region of US$2,300/month on an annual commitment, with a variable component tied to GMV. Adobe Commerce licences are quoted privately and scale with gross merchandise value; industry practitioners consistently report annual figures spanning roughly US$22,000 to well over US$120,000 before hosting or implementation. Neither figure is the important one.


The important one is the run rate. An Adobe Commerce build typically requires a dedicated retainer covering security patches, Adobe's quarterly release cadence, PHP version upgrades, and infrastructure monitoring. Adobe's own developer documentation sets out the upgrade compatibility and patch process in detail ([Adobe Commerce Developer Documentation](https://developer.adobe.com/commerce/docs/) ). On Shopify, the equivalent obligation is checking that your apps survive platform updates — materially cheaper, materially less flexible.


In APAC there is a third cost line that gets missed entirely: developer supply. Senior Adobe Commerce engineers in Hong Kong, Singapore and Taipei are a thin market. Shopify and front-end JavaScript talent is not. If you build something only three people in your city can maintain, you have created a commercial risk, not a technical one.


### 2. Localisation depth, market by market


This is where the APAC lens actually changes the answer.


Shopify Markets lets you run multiple countries from a single store with local currencies, domains, pricing rules and duty handling. Shopify Payments availability, however, remains uneven across Asia — it is live in Singapore, Hong Kong and Australia but absent in several ASEAN markets, which means falling back to third-party gateways and accepting an additional transaction fee on top of the subscription. Check current coverage against Shopify's payments documentation before you model the economics, because this list changes.


Adobe Commerce handles multi-store, multi-locale natively through website/store/store-view scoping, and it will accept any payment gateway someone is willing to write a module for. That matters when you need Touch 'n Go or DuitNow in Malaysia, PromptPay in Thailand, QRIS in Indonesia, or Alipay HK and FPS in Hong Kong. Regional aggregators such as 2C2P and Adyen reduce the gap on Shopify, but the integration effort sits in different places.


One concrete example of the scoping difference. On Adobe Commerce, setting a Traditional Chinese store view for Hong Kong is a CLI operation:


```text
1  bin/magento config:set general/locale/code zh_Hant_HK --scope=stores --scope-code=hk_zh    2  bin/magento config:set currency/options/default HKD --scope=websites --scope-code=hk    3  bin/magento config:set currency/options/allow HKD,CNY --scope=websites --scope-code=hk    4  bin/magento indexer:reindex    5  bin/magento cache:flush
```


Every attribute, price, CMS block and tax rule can then be overridden at website, store or store-view level. It is genuinely powerful and genuinely slow to administer. Shopify's equivalent is configuration in the Markets UI plus a metafield strategy — faster to set up, harder to bend when a single market needs a rule that contradicts the global model.


### 3. Integration surface: ERP, POS, and marketplaces


APAC retail is multi-channel by default. A brand in this region typically runs physical stores, its own site, Lazada, Shopee, and often TikTok Shop or a marketplace storefront in a second country. Whichever platform you pick, the integration layer decides whether inventory is trustworthy.


Shopify's advantage is the app marketplace and a stable, well-documented Admin GraphQL API ([Shopify Developer Documentation](https://shopify.dev/docs) ). A middleware pattern — Shopify as the storefront and order source of truth, an iPaaS or custom service syncing to SAP, Oracle NetSuite, or a local ERP — is well-trodden. Example of the query shape you would use to pull unfulfilled orders for an ERP sync:


```text
1  query UnfulfilledOrders($cursor: String) {    2    orders(first: 50, after: $cursor, query: "fulfillment_status:unfulfilled") {    3      pageInfo { hasNextPage endCursor }    4      edges {    5        node {    6          id    7          name    8          createdAt    9          currentTotalPriceSet { shopMoney { amount currencyCode } }    10          shippingAddress { countryCodeV2 city }    11          lineItems(first: 50) {    12            edges { node { sku quantity } }    13          }    14        }    15      }    16    }    17  }
```


Adobe Commerce's advantage is that the integration can live inside the application. If your pricing logic depends on ERP-held contract terms that change daily, you can implement that as a plugin against the price model rather than pre-computing it upstream. Whether that is a feature or a liability depends entirely on whether you want business logic in your commerce platform at all.


My general position, formed from building these systems for listed retail groups in Greater China: keep business logic out of the storefront wherever possible. Storefronts get replatformed. ERPs do not.


### 4. Speed of change for non-technical teams


This is the axis executives consistently undervalue and marketing teams consistently rate highest. On Shopify, a merchandiser can launch a campaign page, adjust a collection, and change checkout upsell rules in an afternoon. On Adobe Commerce, Page Builder has improved this considerably, but the practical reality in most implementations is that meaningful changes route through a development queue.


Over 36 months, that difference compounds into dozens of campaigns shipped versus dozens deferred. Nobody puts it in the business case. Everybody feels it.


### 5. Risk, compliance, and exit


Shopify is PCI DSS Level 1 certified and carries the compliance burden for you. On Adobe Commerce you own the hosting environment's security posture, even on Adobe Commerce on Cloud, and you own patching. Baymard Institute's ongoing checkout research consistently finds that the largest conversion losses come from checkout friction rather than platform capability ([Baymard Institute](https://baymard.com/) ) — which is a reminder that the compliance-heavy build often wins on control and loses on the metric that pays the bills.


On exit: Shopify's lock-in is real but shallower than people assume — product, customer and order data export cleanly. Adobe Commerce's lock-in is the custom code, not the data.

## Where a Multi-Market ASEAN Rollout Actually Breaks


We worked with a Malaysia-headquartered value retail chain operating hundreds of physical stores across several ASEAN markets. The platform question was not the hard part. The hard part was that store-level inventory, franchise-adjacent regional operations, and three different last-mile carriers all needed to reconcile against one online catalogue with market-specific SKUs and market-specific pricing.


What we learned generalises. The failure modes in APAC cross-border rollouts are, in rough order of frequency:


- **Catalogue divergence.** Market teams create local SKUs off-system. Within a year the "single catalogue" is four catalogues wearing a trench coat.
- **Payment reconciliation.** Each local gateway settles on a different cycle in a different currency. Finance cannot close the month.
- **Address and phone validation.** Western-designed address forms do not handle Hong Kong building/floor/flat, Japanese postal ordering, or Indonesian kelurahan structures. Failed deliveries follow.
- **Tax and duty.** Shifting de minimis thresholds across the region make landed-cost display a moving target.


Neither Shopify nor Adobe Commerce solves any of these for you. Shopify gets you to the first transaction faster; Adobe Commerce gives you more room to model the mess once you understand it. Choosing before you have mapped the mess is the actual mistake.


## When to Choose Shopify Plus


Pick Shopify Plus when most of these are true:


- Your revenue is predominantly D2C or simple wholesale, and Shopify's B2B features (company accounts, price lists, payment terms) cover your buyer workflows.
- You operate in three to ten markets and want them running inside twelve weeks, not twelve months.
- Your team is marketing-led and needs to change merchandising weekly.
- Your custom logic can live in Shopify Functions, headless front ends (Hydrogen or a Next.js storefront on the Storefront API), or middleware — not in the platform core.
- You want the security and PCI burden off your balance sheet.
- You cannot reliably hire and retain three or more senior back-end engineers in your market.


The honest trade-off: you will eventually hit something Shopify will not let you do, and you will route around it with an app or middleware at additional cost. Also, app sprawl is a real tax — twenty apps at US$50–300/month each adds up to a meaningful line item, and each one is a dependency you do not control.

## When to Choose Adobe Commerce


Pick Adobe Commerce when most of these are true:


- You run a dealer, distributor, or franchise network where each account has negotiated pricing, credit terms, and catalogue visibility, and these rules change frequently.
- Your products are configurable in ways that generate large SKU matrices, or you need quote-to-order as a first-class workflow.
- You already run Adobe Experience Manager, Analytics, or Real-Time CDP and the integration value is real rather than theoretical.
- You have regulatory or data-residency requirements that demand control over the hosting environment.
- You have budget for a standing engineering team, not just a launch budget. Adobe ships security patches and quarterly releases; an unpatched Commerce instance is a liability, as the well-documented history of Magento vulnerabilities makes clear.


The honest trade-off: every quarter you do not upgrade, your upgrade cost rises. Teams that treat Adobe Commerce as a build-and-forget asset end up on an unsupported version within three years and facing a replatform they did not budget for.


## What About BigCommerce, WooCommerce, and SHOPLINE?


The Magento vs Shopify vs WooCommerce comparison is a different conversation. WooCommerce dominates by raw site count — BuiltWith's platform tracking consistently shows WordPress-based commerce leading on installed base ([BuiltWith](https://trends.builtwith.com/shop) ) — but installed base and enterprise suitability are not the same measure. WooCommerce is excellent for content-led brands with modest catalogues and in-house WordPress skills; it becomes an operations burden at multi-market scale.


BigCommerce sits between the two majors: more open than Shopify on templating and API limits, less demanding than Adobe Commerce. Its APAC market presence and partner depth are thinner, which matters when you need local implementation support.


SHOPLINE deserves serious consideration for Greater China, Taiwan, Hong Kong and parts of Southeast Asia. Its native handling of social commerce, livestream selling, LINE and WhatsApp integrations, and local payment methods reflects how the region actually buys. If more than half your GMV originates in a chat app or a live session, a Western platform is fighting your business model.

## The Decision Framework


Run these five questions in order. Stop at the first decisive answer.


### Question 1: Where does your complexity live?


If complexity lives in *pricing and buyer relationships* (dealer tiers, contracts, quotes), Adobe Commerce has the edge. If it lives in *channels and markets* (many countries, many storefronts, many campaigns), Shopify has the edge. If it lives in *supply chain* , neither platform is the answer — fix the ERP first.


### Question 2: Can you fund permanent engineering?


Not a launch team. A standing capability of at least two to three engineers with Adobe Commerce depth, retained for the life of the platform. If the answer is no, Adobe Commerce will degrade into technical debt regardless of how well it is built. This single question resolves the decision for most mid-market APAC retailers.


### Question 3: What is your realistic change velocity requirement?


Count the merchandising and campaign changes your team wants to make per month. If it is over twenty, platform agility outweighs platform depth.


### Question 4: What is the 36-month TCO, fully loaded?


Licence or subscription, hosting, implementation, apps or extensions, integration middleware, and annual maintenance at a realistic percentage of build cost. Compare like for like. Most Shopify-versus-Adobe business cases I see understate Adobe's maintenance line and understate Shopify's app line.


### Question 5: What breaks if you are wrong?


Replatforming from Shopify is expensive. Replatforming from a heavily customised Adobe Commerce instance is expensive *and* slow, because the business logic has to be archaeologically recovered from the code. Weight the reversibility.


## Where This Is Heading


The interesting shift is that this comparison is becoming less binary. Composable architecture means the storefront, checkout, search, CMS, and order management can now come from different vendors, and both Shopify and Adobe are repositioning around APIs rather than monoliths — Adobe through API Mesh and App Builder, Shopify through Hydrogen, Functions, and an expanding Storefront API surface. Gartner's Peer Insights listings for digital commerce show both vendors rated closely by practitioners ([Gartner Peer Insights](https://www.gartner.com/reviews/market/digital-commerce) ), which tells you the gap is now about fit, not quality.


What I expect over the next two to three years in APAC: AI-assisted merchandising and agentic checkout will widen Shopify's lead in speed-to-value for consumer brands, while Adobe Commerce consolidates around genuinely complex B2B and manufacturer-dealer models where the commerce layer must hold the logic. The middle ground — mid-sized retailers who chose Adobe Commerce in 2018 because it was the enterprise default — will keep migrating. That migration, not the greenfield decision, is where most of the regional activity will be.


If you are running a Shopify vs Adobe Commerce platform comparison right now, spend one week on the platforms and three weeks on your data model, your ERP integration contract, and your market-by-market payment stack. That is where the outcome is actually decided.
